body: Nigeria's Street View often shows the Google car, which is a pickup truck. The truck's appearance varies, but a roof rack is common in Generation 3 coverage. Sometimes, the entire truck is blurred out.
A police car escort, usually white or black, is a very common sight in Nigerian Street View.
Nigerian license plates are short and often have a greenish tint when blurred.
Nigerian utility poles are typically concrete with indentations and horizontal supports. They resemble Brazilian poles but lack the holes going through them.
Nigerian roads often show signs of poor maintenance. It is common to see roads with faded or no lines, potholes, cracks, or unpaved surfaces.
Typical Nigerian houses are single-story buildings with steep, metal roofs. Many are enclosed by cinder block walls.
Look for city and state names on storefronts and banners. This is a common and useful clue in Nigeria.
Nigeria is unique in mainland Africa for its low-quality "ari" or "shitcam" Street View coverage.
Nigeria is mostly flat, with some hills in the southeast and southwest. The north has more prominent hills and mountains, especially in the east, though they are rarely seen in Street View.

Nigeria's climate shifts from tropical rainforest in the south to savanna in the center and arid steppe in the far north. Be aware that seasonal changes can make the landscape appear greener or drier than typical for the climate zone.
Street View coverage in Nigeria is sparse, mainly focused on major cities and connecting highways. The northwest and east have very little coverage.
Generation 3 coverage is not found north of Abuja, and Generation 4 is absent in the northwest and far south. Low-quality "shitcam" can be found in most of Nigeria.
Certain Nigerian states have uniquely colored vehicles and tuk-tuks. For example, some states feature yellow tuk-tuks.
Southern Nigeria is predominantly Christian, while the north is mainly Islamic. Consequently, Islamic attire is more common to see in the northern regions.
Distinctive haystacks are a very strong clue for being in Kaduna state.
An arid, green, agricultural landscape with lots of corn is characteristic of Kano state. This area only has low-quality "shitcam" coverage.
Benue state features lush green grass, reddish soil, and scattered trees. Thatched huts are also common, but an abundance of palm trees suggests a neighboring southern state instead.
Niger state is characterized by low-quality "shitcam" coverage, scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass. It's like a drier version of Benue state.
The northwestern states (Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, Katsina) have a very open and arid landscape with sparse or no trees. This region is covered exclusively by "shitcam".
A savanna landscape with rocky hills is common in the northeastern states. The hills are generally greener on the eastern and western sides of this region.
Large, monolithic mountains with exposed, weathered rock are a common feature in and around the capital, Abuja.
East of Lekki, the landscape is flat and sandy with coastal vegetation and many palm trees. The coverage is mostly old Generation 3 and features a silver follow car.
The A121 is a divided highway with lush tropical vegetation and a narrow concrete median. It's a busy road, but be aware that the A232 east of Benin City is similar but has a wider median.
North of Takum towards Jalingo, you'll find a dry, hazy Generation 3 landscape with distant mountains. A noticeable smudge appears at the front of the camera in this area.
The A3 highway east of Potiskum features Generation 4 coverage, a divided highway, and a mostly open, arid landscape.
Unusually dark red soil is a strong clue for the areas around Benin City and Enugu.
The Obudu Plateau road features the tallest mountains in Nigerian Street View. Expect a winding road through lush, green mountains with foggy and wet conditions.
A specific type of low-quality "shitcam" coverage with a noticeable blue tint appears in certain areas of Nigeria.
While uncommon, different old Generation 3 follow cars can help pinpoint your location in Nigeria. A rare silver Lexus can sometimes be spotted on the highway between Onitsha and Enugu.
